# slack_app (Resource)

Manage a Slack App using its complete manifest. Updates replace the entire app configuration. Destroy permanently deletes the app. Credentials returned during creation are stored in state and cannot be recovered by import.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "slack_app" "notifications" {
  manifest = jsonencode({
    display_information = {
      name        = "Notifications"
      description = "Deployment notifications"
    }
    features = {
      bot_user = {
        display_name  = "Notifications"
        always_online = false
      }
    }
    oauth_config = {
      scopes = {
        bot = ["chat:write"]
      }
    }
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `manifest` (String) Complete app manifest as a JSON object string. Use jsonencode, or jsonencode(yamldecode(file(...))). Unknown Slack fields are passed through. JSON whitespace and object key order are insignificant.

### Read-Only

- `client_id` (String) OAuth client ID returned at creation. Null for imported apps.
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) OAuth client secret returned at creation. Stored in state; null for imported apps. External rotation cannot be detected.
- `exported_manifest` (String) Last complete manifest exported by Slack, including server defaults. Used to detect remote changes without recurring diffs from defaults.
- `id` (String) Slack App ID. Import using this ID.
- `oauth_authorize_url` (String) Initial authorization URL returned at creation. Not refreshed after scope changes; null for imported apps.
- `signing_secret` (String, Sensitive) Signing secret returned at creation. Stored in state; null for imported apps. External rotation cannot be detected.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing Slack App by its App ID.
terraform import slack_app.notifications A0123456789
```
